The 10% applicant contribution is an eligibility and cost-share constraint, not a default 90% grant formula.

repairs.evidenceText: Reviewed uploaded RetroFi package context.  The current OER page says the Agricultural Energy Grant Program provides grants up to $20,000 for eligible farm energy efficiency and renewable energy projects, awards are subject to funds and OER sole discretion, application submission does not guarantee an award, and applications are accepted on a rolling basis with a 5:00pm Friday, November 6, 2026 due date. ([Rhode Island Office of Energy Resources][1]) The guidance states qualified Rhode Island agribusinesses may be eligible for grants up to $20,000, application submission does not guarantee an award, all awards are subject to funding availability, applicants must contribute at least 10% of total project costs, and awards are based on highest-to-lowest ranking scores.  The guidance lists eligible technologies, ineligible completed/interconnected projects, audit and feasibility-study requests, and REG renewable energy projects; it also states the $20,000 cap is per applicant per calendar year, funds are for direct materials and labor, and grants are competitive.   Payment evidence supports reimbursement treatment: awardees must provide paid-cost documentation, costs before an executed OER contract are not reimbursable, initial and final payments are split 50/50, and final payment requires post-inspection.   The guidance states qualified applications are reviewed and scored, funded from highest to lowest scoring, exact funding amounts are at OER sole discretion, and successful applicants receive an award letter indicating the amount awarded.  The energy efficiency and renewable application forms request total project cost, other funding, applicant contribution of at least 10%, a requested RI Agricultural Energy Program amount of $20,000 or less, and a zero shortfall; the attestations state disbursement requires proof of full funding and OER MOU and is subject to OER discretion and availability of funds.   The dashboard was last updated June 30, 2026 and shows historical awarded-program metrics, while not providing applications submitted, current round budget, expected award count, or success-rate evidence. ([Rhode Island Office of Energy Resources][2])  DEM confirms the OER/DEM program provides grant awards up to $20,000 for eligible farm energy efficiency and renewable energy projects. ([RIDEM][3]) ACE TAP audits are free technical assistance, not a cash grant award value. ([Rhode Island Office of Energy Resources][4])
repairs.reasoningNotes: This package should remain suppressed for user-facing totals. The official sources support an active 2026 round and a $20,000 maximum request/award cap, but not a deterministic award, not a 90% reimbursement formula, and not a defensible expected value. The application request amount is not an award amount. Historical awarded-project data does not establish probability without an application denominator or current award budget. A conditional cash value can be validated only after an official OER award letter or executed agreement is available and reimbursement gates are satisfied.

repairs.programName: Alaska - National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) Formula Grant Program

conditionalAwardModel.formulaText: Do not estimate from eligibility, project cost, or the 80% federal cost-share ceiling alone. Calculate only for a project with a current Alaska NEVI RFA, selection notice, award letter, or executed project grant agreement and application_or_award_status in selected, approved, or executed_grant_agreement. Runtime conditional_award_cents = min(approved_award_amount_cents, round(eligible_project_cost_cents * 0.80)). Return null and suppress if approved_award_amount_cents is missing, eligible_project_cost_cents is missing, non_federal_match_cents is less than 20% of eligible_project_cost_cents, total federal share after stacking would exceed 80%, the scope is not NEVI-compliant public EV charging infrastructure, or costs were incurred before the required award/agreement/authorization/notice-to-proceed.

Verify non_federal_match_cents >= ceil(eligible_project_cost_cents * 0.20) and total federal share after stacking <= 80%; otherwise return null and suppress.

repairs.evidenceText: Uploaded package context reviewed: . AEA states FHWA approved Alaska's FY26 Electric Vehicle Implementation Plan on October 10, 2025, that Alaska is eligible to obligate over $52 million in FY22-FY26 NEVI formula funding, and that Phase 1 covers 2025-2026 while Phase 2 covers 2026-2028. ([AK Energy Authority][1]) The FY26 plan lists Alaska's FY22-FY26 NEVI formula allocation as $52,415,294, describes a competitive RFA for EVSE at up to 14 AFC sites, requires separate project grant agreements for chosen sites, and states payments will be made monthly or quarterly on a reimbursement schedule tied to milestones and deliverables. ([AK Energy Authority][2]) FHWA guidance states the federal cost share for NEVI projects is 80%, allows private and state funds to provide the non-federal share, permits contracting with private entities for acquisition, installation, operations, and maintenance, and caps total federal cost share at 80%. ([Federal Highway Administration][3]) The FY26 plan estimates $43,870,634 available for Phase 2 construction after remaining administration funding, but describes that figure as a program planning estimate rather than a per-project entitlement or open application window. ([AK Energy Authority][4]) AEA's active solicitation page checked for current applicant-facing opportunities listed only RFI#AIDEA26-050 for the AIDEA hangar and did not list an Alaska NEVI RFA. ([AIDEA/AEA Procurement][5]) AEA's 2023 update reported 34 Phase 1 applications and projects selected in nine communities with $6.4 million federal NEVI funding matched by $1.6 million from private entities; that history is not a current-round applicant probability.  AEA's April 2026 board packet/newsletter material says FHWA certified Alaska's AFC as fully built out and that Alaska can now move into Phase 2, supporting upcoming Phase 2 treatment but not a current user-facing award estimate. ([AK Energy Authority][6])
repairs.reasoningNotes: Repair outcome: keep the package suppressed by default. The program is real and funded at the state level, but the applicant-facing calculation is not deterministic without a site-specific RFA or award document. The 80% NEVI share is a reimbursement ceiling, not an expected value. The public active procurement page did not show a current Alaska NEVI RFA, and the Phase 2 materials found describe planning and authority to proceed rather than a posted solicitation with deadlines, scoring, caps, and award count. Current Phase 1 history should be retained as context only and not converted into a probability discount.
humanReviewReasons: No current open Alaska NEVI RFA was found on the public AIDEA/AEA active solicitation page.
Future Phase 2 solicitation terms, deadlines, scoring criteria, site counts, per-project caps, and eligible-cost rules were not found in a current RFA.
Competitive selection requires a project-specific selection notice, award letter, or executed project grant agreement.
Approved award amount and approved eligible project cost basis are required before calculating a value.
Non-federal match and total federal cost-share stacking must be reviewed against the current award documents.
Historical 34-applications/nine-communities evidence is not a defensible current applicant-level probability.

conditionalAwardModel.formulaText: Conditional reimbursement only after reservation approval and eligible installation: station_rebate = min(max(0, eligible_charger_equipment_and_installation_cost_cents - other_rebates_or_tax_credits_for_same_station_cents), charger_count * per_charger_cap_cents), where per_charger_cap_cents is 350000 for general public-access Level 2 or higher locations and 750000 for schools, income-qualified affordable housing MUD locations, or publicly accessible DC fast plug-in locations. Add submeter_rebate = min(submeter_install_cost_cents, 350000) if an associated sub-meter rebate is requested and eligible. Add plan_check_rebate = min(city_plan_check_fee_cents, 150000). Apply max 10 charging stations per customer per year. Apply customer cap: 2500000 cents for commercial customers, or 4000000 cents for school or affordable housing multi-unit dwelling locations. Do not treat any 'up to' amount as expected value.

repairs.programName: Anoka Municipal Utility - Commercial Energy Efficiency Rebate Program

conditionalAwardModel.formulaText: For eligible AMU commercial customers, calculate only from the applicable published measure formula, then apply the applicable 60%/$100,000 cap. Retrofit lighting: for each row, annual kWh savings = ((removed fixture count × removed watts per fixture × removed annual hours) - (new fixture count × new watts per fixture × new annual hours)) / 1000; multiply by 1.1 only if the new lighting is in an air-conditioned area; sum row kWh savings; rebate estimate = total kWh savings × $0.10, capped at the lesser of 60% of eligible lighting equipment cost excluding labor or $100,000. New lighting: source confirms AMU calculates from estimated kWh savings using TRM baseline/annual hours, but public materials reviewed do not provide a complete user-side worksheet equivalent to the retrofit worksheet; do not auto-calculate new-lighting rebates unless the estimator has the current TRM baseline mapping and AMU-approved method. Commercial DX cooling: per unit rebate = ($15 × nominal tons) + ($3 × ((equipment SEER2/EER2/IEER2 value - applicable minimum qualifying efficiency) / 0.1) × nominal tons), subject to table thresholds and caps. Rooftop-unit economizer: rebate = $15 × RTU tons × number of units, only where both enthalpy and CO2 controls qualify. Cooling rebates are capped at the lesser of 60% of project cost including equipment and labor or $100,000, and cannot exceed the equipment purchase price. Custom/non-listed measures require AMU review/approval and should not be auto-estimated from the cap alone.

repairs.programName: Commercial Scale Renewable Energy Grants (Commerce RI)

conditionalAwardModel.formulaText: Do not calculate unless the project is in Rhode Island, is net-metered for on-site load or an eligible nonprofit PPA/off-taker structure, does not use virtual net metering, does not participate in the Renewable Energy Growth program, is direct ownership or eligible nonprofit TPO, has not been installed partially or completely before REF approval, has a complete application, and has current-round funding and installer/block cap availability confirmed. Base PV award cents = min(7500000, 70 * min(pv_dc_watts_total, 50000) + 40 * min(max(pv_dc_watts_total - 50000, 0), 50000) + 30 * min(max(pv_dc_watts_total - 100000, 0), 50000) + 20 * min(max(pv_dc_watts_total - 150000, 0), 50000)). No base PV rate is modeled beyond 200 kW because the June 2026 Commercial RFP shows '-' for D.O. in the 201 kW and up row. Solar carport adder cents = 55 * solar_carport_dc_watts, including eligible carport capacity above 200 kW if applicable. If solar_carport_dc_watts > 0, solar/carport award cents = min(base_pv_award_cents + solar_carport_adder_cents, 20000000, installer_carport_block_cap_remaining_cents). If solar_carport_dc_watts = 0, base solar award cents = min(base_pv_award_cents, 7500000, installer_base_block_cap_remaining_cents). Commercial storage adder is separate and only calculable after storage adder application review/approval: storage_three_hour_continuous_power_watts = min(storage_total_battery_capacity_wh / 3, storage_inverter_max_continuous_power_watts); storage_adder_cents = min(50 * storage_three_hour_continuous_power_watts, 4000000). Total conditional award cents = solar_or_solar_carport_award_cents + approved_storage_adder_cents. Do not use the flyer statement that grants could cover up to 30% of renewable energy installation costs as a grant formula.

ineligibleCostCategories: projects outside Rhode Island

renewable generation output counted toward the storage three-hour continuous power rating
roofing work or other costs indirectly related to the solar project when reporting total project cost

requiredInputs.whyNeeded: Projects must be located in Rhode Island.
Commercial REF projects must be net-metered systems serving on-site load or eligible nonprofit off-takers under a PPA structure.
Projects using virtual net metering are not eligible.
REF cannot be combined with the Renewable Energy Growth program for the same project.
The current RFP supports direct ownership and a nonprofit-only third-party ownership exception.
Eligible sectors include businesses, institutions, nonprofits, municipalities, and state facilities.
Incentives are only available for systems not installed partially or completely before REF approval.
The next listed commercial round date is needed because dates are approximate and blocks can close when funds are reached.
User-facing totals should not include this incentive before award letter, executed grant agreement, completion/inspection, or payment status is documented.
All awards are subject to availability of funds, and current remaining funds were not found in public program text.
Base commercial awards are subject to a $150,000 cap per block per installer.
Solar carport awards are subject to a $600,000 cap per block per installer.
The base commercial REF award is calculated from rated DC capacity by watt tiers.
The solar carport adder is calculated at $0.55 per eligible carport DC watt and capped separately.
The storage adder should be skipped when no energy storage component is in the project scope.
The commercial storage adder uses total battery capacity in Wh divided by three hours.
The commercial storage adder uses the lesser of battery Wh divided by three hours and inverter maximum continuous power in W.
The storage component must meet Rhode Island Energy Connected Solutions technical eligibility, with enrollment, non-Rhode-Island-Energy-customer, or owner opt-out documentation as applicable.
All energy storage adder applications are subject to review and approval.

calculationTraceTemplate: Confirm RI location, net metering, no VNM, no REG participation, eligible sector, and direct ownership or nonprofit-only TPO eligibility.
Confirm project was not installed partially or completely before REF approval and that required application documents are complete.
Confirm the applicable commercial round date, current funding availability, and remaining installer/block cap amounts before calculating any user-facing value.

Calculate base PV cents from the June 2026 RFP: 70 cents/W for first 50 kW, 40 cents/W for second 50 kW, 30 cents/W for third 50 kW, and 20 cents/W for fourth 50 kW, capped at $75,000/project and $150,000/block/installer.

Calculate solar carport adder cents as 55 cents per eligible carport DC watt; for carport projects cap the total solar/carport request at $200,000/project and the applicable installer/block cap at $600,000.

Calculate storage three-hour continuous power as min(total battery Wh / 3, inverter maximum continuous W); storage adder cents = min(50 cents/W * storage power W, $40,000), only after storage adder approval.
Suppress pre-award expected value because no public application denominator or success probability was found and public remaining-funds/block-cap data is not sufficient.

probabilityModel.probabilityNotes: Do not calculate a probability-discounted expected value. stackingRules.stackingNotes: REF cannot be paired with Rhode Island Energy's Renewable Energy Growth program for the same project. Official REF materials say the program can be paired with the federal tax credit, but the grant estimate should not include any federal tax credit value; for REF application cost reporting, the application says total project cost should not account for tax incentives, grants, or other cash incentives.

repairs.evidenceText: The uploaded RetroFi package context was reviewed for this repair.  Commerce RI’s REF page identifies REF as a renewable energy grant program and lists 2026 commercial scale rounds, including a 26-2 commercial date of July 31, 2026 and a 26-3 commercial date of October 23, 2026; it also says commercial blocks close on the application closing date or when available funds have been reached. ([Commerce RI][1]) The June 2026 Commercial-Scale RFP requires RI location, net metering, no REG pairing, no VNM, direct ownership with a nonprofit-only TPO exception, and no partial or complete installation before REF approval. ([Cloudinary][2]) The June 2026 RFP provides the repaired commercial rate table: base D.O./eligible nonprofit TPO rates of $0.70/W, $0.40/W, $0.30/W, and $0.20/W for the first four 50 kW tiers, a $0.55/W solar carport adder, $75,000 base cap, $200,000 carport project cap, $150,000 and $600,000 installer/block caps, and $40,000 storage cap; the same page says funding is subject to availability. ([Cloudinary][2]) The commercial application caps REF amount requested at $75,000, or $200,000 for solar carport projects, asks for total project cost without accounting for tax incentives, grants, or other cash incentives, and captures DC system rating without rounding. ([Cloudinary][3]) The storage RFP and storage addendum support $0.50/W based on the maximum continuous power rating deliverable over three hours, capped at $40,000, calculated as the lesser of total battery Wh divided by three hours and inverter maximum continuous W, and subject to Connected Solutions eligibility, review, approval, and funding availability.  The active RI rule confirms Commercial Scale as a REF program area, says applications are accepted only during open solicitations, states funding is issued as grants, work may begin after contract execution, and construction grants are paid after successful completion and inspection. ([Rhode Island Department of State][4]) The 2025 annual report lists 70 approved commercial solar projects totaling $2,148,875, plus two storage adder awards and two carport adder grants, but it does not provide total applications or a success-rate denominator.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Use the June 2026 Commercial RFP as the controlling commercial rate source where it differs from the April 2026 flyer or April RFP. Remove unsupported third-party-ownership half-rate rows; current official materials support direct ownership and a nonprofit-only TPO exception. Treat the solar carport $200,000 limit as a total solar/carport project request cap because the commercial application says REF amount requested for solar carport projects is not to exceed $200,000. Suppress user-facing totals until project-specific scope, REF award status, funding availability, and installer/block cap remaining are confirmed. No probability discount is defensible from public official sources.

repairs.programName: Community EV Chargers Incentive Program

conditionalAwardModel.formulaText: For a currently eligible Level 1 or Level 2 workplace or multi-unit residence project with funds confirmed available for the site county and track, estimate the grant as the lesser of: eligible total project cost times the applicable coverage rate, applicable component caps, applicable per-location project cap, applicant remaining cap, and confirmed remaining county/track funds. Coverage is 100% only where the program match is 0%, 95% where the required match is 5%, and 90% where the required match is 10%. Component caps are Level 1 hardware $500 per port and make-ready/installation $3,600; Level 2 OCPP hardware $3,000 per port, Level 2 non-OCPP hardware $2,000 per port, and make-ready/installation $20,000. Project caps are $5,600/$7,600/$9,600 for Level 1 or $32,000/$44,000/$56,000 for Level 2 based on the 4/8/12-port workplace or multi-unit size tier. The applicant cap for Level 1 and Level 2 incentives is $100,000. Public Attraction Level 2 and DCFC should not be estimated unless a current source separately verifies reopened funding.

probabilityModel.probabilityNotes: This is not a scored competitive expected-value estimate for the active Level 1/Level 2 tracks; it is first-come/first-served and funding-constrained. State testimony reports 610 applications processed from July 2023 through December 2025, 70 completed projects and 21 in construction, about 200 applications on hold due to fully subscribed funds, and $6.804 million for rolling Level 1/Level 2 incentives after an August 2025 funding increase, but those figures do not support a defensible probability discount for an individual project without current county/track availability.

repairs.programName: Efficiency Works - Business Energy Efficiency Rebate Program (Offered by 4 Utilities)

conditionalAwardModel.formulaText: Community Efficiency Grant additional incentive = min(standard_rebate_cents, max(0, eligible_project_cost_cents - standard_rebate_cents)). The combined standard rebate plus Community Efficiency Grant cannot exceed 100% of eligible project cost. Standard rebate caps and requirements apply. The CEG pathway is only available for qualifying nonprofit community service providers and income-qualified multifamily properties, requires preapproval, excludes custom incentives, electric vehicle charging infrastructure, Building Tune-up incentives, and all study incentives, and remains subject to funding availability.

Efficiency Works Business electric incentives are limited to commercial electric customers of Estes Park Power and Communications, Fort Collins Utilities, Longmont Power & Communications, or City of Loveland Utilities.
The underlying measure must be eligible for a standard rebate and cannot fall into excluded categories such as custom, EV charging infrastructure, Building Tune-up, or study incentives.
CEG eligibility depends on whether the applicant qualifies as a nonprofit critical community service provider or an income-qualified multifamily property.
For the nonprofit pathway, the application requires IRS 501(c)(3) status in good standing and listing in the Colorado charity search.
For the nonprofit pathway, the organization must provide a qualifying critical community service or submit an Other justification subject to program review.
For the multifamily pathway, income qualification requires verification that the property meets the 66% at or below 80% AMI requirement or an accepted equivalent pathway.
The CEG requires project preapproval after January 1, 2026 and before materials are ordered or work begins.
The 2026 CEG requires project completion and all final paperwork before November 15, 2026.
Grant funds are limited, first-come, first-served, and no live remaining-funds balance was found in the checked public sources.

calculationTraceTemplate: Confirm the project site is a commercial electric customer of one of the four eligible Efficiency Works utilities.
Confirm the project measure is eligible for a standard Efficiency Works Business rebate and is not in an excluded CEG category.
Confirm the applicant qualifies through the nonprofit critical community service pathway or the income-qualified multifamily pathway.
Confirm CEG preapproval occurred after 2026-01-01 and before materials were ordered or work began.
Calculate the standard Efficiency Works Business rebate under the applicable measure rules and caps.
Set preliminary CEG additional incentive equal to standard_rebate_cents.
Apply the project-cost cap: final CEG = min(preliminary CEG, max(0, eligible_project_cost_cents - standard_rebate_cents)).
Return no user-facing dollar estimate unless standard rebate, eligible cost, eligibility approval, deadline compliance, and funding availability are all confirmed.

repairs.evidenceText: The uploaded RetroFi package summary for SOURCE_DSIRE:dsire_program_id:22542 was used as the package under repair . Entergy Mississippi's residential tariff page lists NEM-2 Net Energy Metering Rider Schedule and says official tariff documents on file with the Mississippi Public Service Commission prevail over website copies if there is a difference. ([Entergy Mississippi][1]) Entergy's NEM-2 tariff states that Schedule NEM-2 is available first-come, first-served to eligible DGICs until the net-metered capacity cap is reached; residential customers must have DGF capacity no more than 20 kWDC and sized to offset no more than 110% of prior-year annual energy usage; eligible DGF must be on the customer's premises, owned or leased by the customer, and powered by a qualifying renewable energy source. ([Entergy Mississippi][2]) The same NEM-2 tariff states that a one-time $3,000 cash LMI Incentive is available to any residential DGIC qualifying as Low-to-Moderate Income who installs eligible renewable DGF, requires proof of installation, a Company-approved energy-efficiency audit before receiving the incentive, DGF nameplate capacity of at least 4 kWDC, and no more than 110% of prior-year annual usage; it is first-come, first-served, subject to annual budget restrictions for calendar years 2023 through 2027, not available beyond 2027, and paid by check or electronic payment after Company inspection/approval and eligibility verification. ([Entergy Mississippi][2]) The tariff budget section states total annual incentive budget is $8 million, LMI Incentive budget is $6 million, Battery Incentive budget is $2 million, budgets do not roll over, and annual budgets are available only for 2023 through 2027. ([Entergy Mississippi][2]) Entergy's Level 1 interconnection application says the Standard Interconnection Agreement must be completed, submitted, and approved before metering is installed for connection to the distribution grid, asks whether the customer is applying for the LMI adder and requires an affidavit, collects proposed kWDC and expected annual generation, and states customer/installer shall not commence parallel operation until Company inspection and approval and meter installation. ([Entergy Mississippi][3]) DSIRE's program result for program 22542 reports that the program is under suspension while the Public Service Commission conducts rulemaking in Docket No. 2025-AD-61. ([DSIRE][4]) The Mississippi PSC docket page lists current 2026 utility dockets, and the July 2026 docket lists 2025-AD-61 as continued, with filing date 6/17/25, in re proposal of the Mississippi Public Service Commission to amend the Mississippi Distributed Generation Rule. ([Mississippi Public Service Commission][5])

([Federal Highway Administration][2]) The federal statute caps the federal share at not more than 80% of total project cost and requires a contracting private entity to pay the non-federal share. ([US Code][3])

repairs.evidenceText: Uploaded](https://www.mdt.mt.gov/publications/plans/ev/%22,%22https://www.mdt.mt.gov/publications/plans/ev/docs/2022-26-NEVI-State-Plan.pdf?v=1%22,%22https://www.mdt.mt.gov/business/contracting/qacurrent.aspx%22,%22https://deq.mt.gov/energy/Programs/fuels%22,%22https://highways.dot.gov/media/73181%22,%22https://highways.dot.gov/laws-regulations/directives/notices/n-4510913%22,%22https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-23/chapter-I/subchapter-G/part-680%22,%22https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/08/13/2025-15370/national-electric-vehicle-infrastructure-formula-program-guidance%22],%22evidenceText%22:%22Uploaded) RetroFi package context reviewed.  MDT states Montana expected approximately $43 million over five years for DC fast chargers along designated Alternative Fuel Corridors, and identifies I-15, I-90, I-94, US-2, and US-93 as Montana AFC routes. ([Montana Department of Transportation][1]) The amended FY2022-2026 Montana EV Infrastructure Deployment Plan states MDT/DEQ selected a Design-Build method, intends to issue competitive two-phase Design-Build solicitations, requires non-State owners/operators to provide the non-Federal match, and says the $900,000 location cost with 80/20 cost share is an assumption until NEVI locations are awarded and built. ([Montana Department of Transportation][2]) MDT's current Q&A for Project EV STWD(983), Control 10436000 says the work includes design, construction, operation, and maintenance of EV charging stations; each station must have at least four network-connected 150 kW DC charging ports, be within approximately one mile of an AFC, be public 24/7 year-round, and provide at least 20% of eligible project cost. ([Montana Department of Transportation][3]) MDT amended the SOQ deadline to April 15, 2026, listed EV Gateway, FTI & SWTCH, and Love's Travel Stops as shortlisted firms, stated MTC will select one NEVI Contractor and MDT will enter into three or more station-specific agreements, and clarified that contractor contribution must be at least 20% and Federal Share of Eligible Costs must not exceed $800,000 for each EV charging station. ([Montana Department of Transportation][3]) FHWA's FY2026 NEVI notice says funds are available until expended, eligible uses include acquisition/installation, O&M up to five years, signs, development, and mapping/analysis, private entities may pay the non-Federal share, and the Federal share payable is 80%; the same notice lists Montana's FY2026 NEVI apportionment as $9,135,437. ([Federal Highway Administration][4]) FHWA Notice N4510.913 later repurposed $12,537,256 of Montana NEVI Formula Program funds, so the currently available Montana NEVI budget for this procurement should not be inferred from the earlier $43 million public summary alone. ([Federal Highway Administration][5]) eCFR Part 680 requires, for corridor DCFC stations, at least four network-connected DCFC ports, 150 kW capability per port, public 24/7 year-round availability, secure payment methods, and five-year charger maintenance compliance. ([eCFR][6])

Tier 1 caps: heating systems $5,700; insulation $17,600 total, with current OHCS application/manual/factsheet subcaps of ceiling/attic $5,900, wall $6,500, floor/subfloor $5,200; windows and doors $5,900; air infiltration $500; occupant health/safety and building-code requirements $1,000. Tier 2 caps: heating systems $3,800; insulation $6,600 total, with ceiling/attic $3,000, wall $1,800, floor/subfloor $1,800; windows and doors $3,000; air infiltration $500; occupant health/safety and building-code requirements $1,000. Total SHOW cash payments over the lifetime of the program for one dwelling may not exceed $30,700, and no unique measure may be claimed more than once.

repairs.evidenceText: Target](https://wisconsindot.gov/Pages/projects/multimodal/electrification.aspx%22,%22https://wisconsindot.gov/Pages/about-wisdot/newsroom/news-rel/052626-WEVI-connecting-corridors.aspx%22,%22https://wisconsindot.gov/Documents/projects/multimodal/WEVI-Connecting-Corridors-RFP.pdf%22,%22https://wisconsindot.gov/Documents/projects/multimodal/WEVI-connecting-corridors-QA.pdf%22,%22https://wisconsindot.gov/Documents/projects/multimodal/WEVI-Submission-Packet.pdf%22,%22https://wisconsindot.gov/Documents/projects/multimodal/WEVI-plan-update-final-9-2024.pdf%22,%22https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-23/chapter-I/subchapter-G/part-680%22,%22https://programs.dsireusa.org/system/program/detail/22650/wisconsin-national-electric-vehicle-infrastructure-nevi-formula-grant-program%22],%22evidenceText%22:%22Target) package was supplied in the uploaded RetroFi prompt file . WisDOT's electrification page states that the WEVI Connecting Corridors RFP was released May 26, 2026 and that all applications must be submitted by July 24, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Central Time ([Wisconsin Department of Transportation][1]). WisDOT's May 26, 2026 release states that proposals are accepted through July 24, awards are expected in fall 2026, approximately $40 million is available in unobligated funds, funding covers up to 80% of eligible costs, and grantees must provide at least 20% non-federal match ([Wisconsin Department of Transportation][2]). The RFP states that WisDOT seeks competitive proposals, provides reimbursement of up to 80% of eligible costs with a minimum 20% non-federal cost share, has no maximum project funding amount, and reimburses only after FHWA authorization, signed final grant agreement, applicable WisDOT notices, approved budgets, paid supplier invoices, and NEVI/23 CFR 680 compliance ([Wisconsin Department of Transportation][3]). The RFP also lists eligible costs and ineligible costs, including exclusion of expenses incurred before formal WisDOT notice or authorization, real estate, major utility grid upgrades, electricity, general staff time, rent, customer service, studies, and lobbying ([Wisconsin Department of Transportation][3]). The July 3, 2026 Q&A confirms no maximum grant amount, no specific total grant amount set for Connecting Corridors, no reimbursement for work before an executed grant agreement, site prior-WEVI-funding exclusions, minimum port and CCS requirements, utility rebates as possible non-federal match, and non-eligibility for the 30C tax credit for Connecting Corridors projects ([Wisconsin Department of Transportation][4]). The 2024 WEVI plan provides historical Round 1 context with 264 applications and 53 awarded sites, but that prior round is not a current-round probability anchor for default user-facing expected value ([Wisconsin Department of Transportation][5]). eCFR 23 CFR Part 680 prescribes NEVI standards and requirements for NEVI-funded projects and publicly accessible EV charger projects funded under Title 23 ([eCFR][6]).
